title: Paloma and the Wolf Again
premise: Marguerite Voss, a bone-carver who hears the dead, has spent her life hidden in a valley where magic cannot follow. When the crown's witch-hunters drag her out, she discovers the dead are whispering one name: the Wolf, an ancient guardian whose slumber keeps a forgotten war buried. Torn between loyalty to the found family of gifted fugitives sheltering her and the truth that one of them is the Wolf reborn, Marguerite must choose whether to silence the dead forever or wake what they guard. In the end, she wakes the Wolf, sacrifices her gift to seal the war away again, and returns home changed — no longer hearing the dead, but finally free.
about_author: Freya Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist from northern Norway who spent a decade cataloguing medieval bone relics before turning to fiction. Her work blends Nordic folklore with quiet, character-driven fantasy about people caught between memory and duty.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the magic-dead valley, Marguerite carves bones for grieving families and hides the voices she hears in them. Crown riders arrive with a proclamation: all gifted must be surrendered. When they seize her sister-figure, young Tamsin, Marguerite reveals her gift to save her — and is taken instead. Emotional beat: protective love shattering a lifetime of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with interludes from hunter-captain Aldric. Marched toward the capital, Marguerite escapes into the wilds and falls in with a band of gifted fugitives led by the enigmatic Rurik, who never dreams and never bleeds. The dead in her carved bones begin repeating a warning: 'the Wolf stirs.' Emotional beat: wary belonging — found family forming even as dread deepens.

chapters.title: The Hunt Turns Homeward
chapters.summary: Rurik's POV. Aldric's hunters corner the fugitives at a ruined shrine; in the battle, Rurik transforms — he is the Wolf, ancient guardian of the sealed war. The dead reveal the crown plans to kill him and claim the old power beneath it. Betrayed by a companion who sold them out, the group scatters, and Marguerite is captured. Emotional beat: love against duty, as Rurik begs her to let him die rather than be used.

chapters.title: Wake the Wolf
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the capital's bone-vault, Marguerite chooses truth over safety: she wakes the Wolf fully before the crown can harness him. The ancient war threatens to reignite until Marguerite pours her gift into sealing it, going deaf to the dead at last. Rurik, mortal now, chooses exile beside her. Emotional beat: sacrifice rewarded not with magic, but with freedom and chosen family.
